sections.content:
Example 3.21

In an international recitation competition of the Holy Quran, a panel of 11 judges is formed to judge the best recitation. Two recitations R_A and R_B were considered to be the best where the opinion of judges got divided. Six judges were in favour of R_A whereas five in favour of R_B. A random sample of five judges was drawn from the panel. Find the probability that out of five judges three are in favour of recitation R_A.

Solution:

In the given problem

n=5, X=0,1,2,3,4,5 \{\because X=0,1,2,\ldots\min(n,k)\}

$p(x)=\left\{\begin{matrix}\dfrac{\binom{6}{x}\binom{11-6}{5-x}}{\binom{N}{n}}, & x=0,1,2,3,4,5\\ 0 & \textit{otherwise}\end{matrix}\right.$

Now

$P(X=3)=\dfrac{\binom{6}{3}\binom{5}{5-3}}{\binom{11}{5}}=\frac{200}{231}$

3.4.3 Properties of hypergeometric probability distribution

◆ Mean of hypergeometric probability distribution by definition is given by

\text{Mean}=E(X)=\sum_x x\,p(x)=\sum_{x=0}^{n}x\dfrac{\binom{k}{x}\binom{N-k}{n-k}}{\binom{N}{n}}

=0\dfrac{\binom{k}{0}\binom{N-k}{n-0}}{\binom{N}{n}}+\sum_{x=1}^{n}x\dfrac{\binom{k}{x}\binom{N-k}{n-k}}{\binom{N}{n}}

=\dfrac{1}{\binom{N}{n}}\sum_{x=1}^{n}x\frac{k!}{(k-x)!\,x!}\binom{N-k}{n-x}

=\dfrac{1}{\binom{N}{n}}\sum_{x=1}^{n}x\frac{k(k-1)!}{(k-x)!\,x(x-1)!}\binom{N-k}{n-x}

=\dfrac{k}{\binom{N}{n}}\sum_{x=1}^{n}\frac{(k-1)!}{(k-x)!\,(x-1)!}\binom{N-k}{n-x}=\dfrac{k}{\binom{N}{n}}\sum_{x=1}^{n}\binom{k-1}{x-1}\binom{N-k}{n-x}

\text{Let } y=x-1\Rightarrow x=y+1

\text{If } x=1,\ y=0

\text{If } x=n,\ y=n-1

\therefore E(X)=\dfrac{k}{\binom{N}{n}}\sum_{y=0}^{n-1}\binom{k-1}{y}\binom{N-k}{n-y-1}

Apply the hypergeometric identity \sum_{r=0}^{k}\binom{m}{r}\binom{n}{k-r}=\binom{m+n}{k}

issues.description: Example 3.21 prints P(X=3) = 200/231; the computed value is C(6,3)C(5,2)/C(11,5) = 200/462 = 100/231. Printed value retained.
The first two lines of the mean derivation print the second binomial as C(N−k, n−k) instead of C(N−k, n−x); printed form retained.
